objects.taxonomy_description: Large shepherd dog with a medium-length double coat in black-and-tan, sable, or solid black. Coat is dense, straight, and close-lying with a thick undercoat. Body is athletic, well-muscled, and slightly longer than tall with a distinctive sloping topline. Head is noble and clean-cut with a broad skull and long, strong muzzle. Ears are large, erect, pointed, and set high. Tail is bushy, reaches to the hock, and carried low with a slight curve. Eyes are medium-sized, almond-shaped, and dark brown with an intelligent, alert expression. The breed's signature features include its erect ears, sloping back, and noble, wolf-like appearance.

objects.taxonomy_description: Stringed instrument with solid or semi-hollow body (no sound hole required). Body shape varies: Stratocaster (double-cutaway, contoured edges), Les Paul (single-cutaway, carved top), Telecaster (single-cutaway, slab body). Body is wood (alder, mahogany, maple) with glossy polyester or nitrocellulose finish in solid colors, sunburst, or natural wood grain. Neck is maple or mahogany with fretted fingerboard (rosewood or maple, 21-24 frets). Pickups (magnetic, 1-3) mounted on body. Control knobs (volume, tone) and pickup selector switch. Bridge is fixed or tremolo. Headstock has 6 tuning pegs. Cable jack on body edge.

objects.taxonomy_description: Domestic swine measuring 90-180 cm body length weighing 50-350 kg. Body stocky and barrel-shaped with sparse coarse bristles over pink, black, or spotted skin. Head large with elongated snout ending in cartilaginous disk for rooting. Eyes small. Ears large and floppy or erect depending on breed. Legs short and stout with cloven hooves. Tail short and curly. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, sparse hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Omnivorous with highly developed olfactory sense.
